Measuring baking soda

A level teaspoon of baking soda weighs about 4.8 g, based on the serving size printed on Arm & Hammer boxes. Some charts list up to 6 g, usually because the soda was packed into the spoon rather than leveled.

Baking soda is about four times stronger than baking powder, so small measuring errors show up quickly as a soapy or metallic taste. Level the spoon with a straight edge, and don't swap soda and powder one for one.

If a recipe lists baking soda in grams, 1 g is a little under ¼ teaspoon.

Source: Arm & Hammer label (⅛ teaspoon = 0.6 g); King Arthur Baking lists 6 g per teaspoon.

Questions

How many grams is 1 tablespoon of baking soda?

1 tablespoon (3 teaspoons) of baking soda weighs about 14 g. A level teaspoon is about 4.8 g.

How many teaspoons is 10 grams of baking soda?

10 g of baking soda is 2⅛ tsp, measured with level spoons.

Is baking soda heavier than baking powder?

Slightly. A level teaspoon of baking soda weighs about 4.8 g and baking powder about 4.6 g. They are not interchangeable, though: baking soda is roughly four times as strong.
